## {.center}

*The landscape is evolving fast and there are many tools*

*This webinar is about communicating concepts*

*Tools are only shown as examples and which tools you chose depends on your OS, how important your data and your system are, and your personal risk tolerance*

## The problem {.center}

Cybersecurity is not new. What changed?

:::{.fragment}

:::{.emph}

AI agents

:::

➔ Bigger risks coming from outside \
➔ Totally novel risks coming from *inside*

:::

## AI agents {.center}

:::{.emph}

AI agent = model + harness

:::

<!-- Non-deterministic and autonomous code execution -->

<!-- unbounded behaviour space -->

:::{.fragment}

### Models

LLMs

Passive text generators

The *intelligent* part

Not a liability in themselves (beside hallucinations and disinformation)

:::

## AI agents {.center}

:::{.emph}

AI agent = model + harness

:::

### Harness

Software infrastructure that turns the LLM into an **actor**

- Set of tools to run code, read files, search the web...
- Context $ memory: info fed to the model
- Guardrails: safety layers such as potential sandboxes (new and flawed)

These function in a loop until a goal is reached:

Reasoning ➔ Actions ➔ Result observation ➔ New actions

## What to worry about? {.center}

Data loss
Compromised system
Privacy
Exposing sensitive data

# Update often

## {.center}

<!-- rolling distros -->
Agents keep finding vulnerabilities

Install patches as soon as they are released

Make sure to update/install from trusted sources

# Backup often

## {.center}

Borg
Rclone
Make sure that backups are encrypted if they are online

# Use version control

# Use a password manager

## {.center}

KeepassXC

- never reuse passwords
- passphrases stronger than passwords
- be mindful of your clipboard and tools using it

# Think about your sensitive data

## {.center}

- Take the time to think about what sensitive data you have where and whether it needs to be where it is

This includes your computer, your phone, your old/broken computers and phones, your backup systems, files on the Alliance systems, your online files (e.g. Google Drive, emails)

Delete sensitive data where it is not needed

- Take the time to think about who has access to your sensitive data and whether they need to have access

Remove access to shared online documents when sharing isn't necessary anymore
Remove access to your files on shared systems to users who don't need access

https://docs.alliancecan.ca/wiki/Sharing_data/en

### At the hardware level

Not using RAM nor CPUs
More secure and more efficient

Hardware Security Module (HSM)
Self-Encrypting Drive (SED)

### Using software

File system encryption

Whole disk encryption

Directories encryption

Files encryption

# Sandbox your agents

## What's a sandbox? {.center}

Does not prevent agents unexpected behaviours but limits their impact zone

## Levels of isolation {.center}

```{dot}
//| echo: false

digraph G {

    // Keeps the arrow perfectly straight

    // REDUCED SPACING:
    // ranksep controls horizontal spacing. Lowering it packs the elements closer.
    ranksep=0.2;
    // nodesep controls vertical spacing between the words, arrow, and boxes.
    nodesep=0.2;
    
    // --- 1. Top Row: Concepts & Spacers ---
    node [shape=plaintext, fontname="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif", fontsize=11];
    Conv [label=<<b>Convenience</b>>, fontcolor="#e67e22"];
    Sec  [label=<<b>Security</b>>, fontcolor="#3973ac"];
    
    // Invisible spacers for the top row (to push the technologies inward)
    node [shape=point, width=0, height=0, style=invis];
    t_OS; t_Cont; t_VM;
    
    // --- 2. Middle Row: Arrow Axis Points ---
    p_Start; p_OS; p_Cont; p_VM; p_End;
    
    // --- 3. Bottom Row: Technologies & Spacers ---
    // Colored boxes for technologies
    node [shape=box, style="rounded", penwidth=2, fontname="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif", fontsize=11];
    OS   [label="OS-level",  color="#cc9900", fontcolor="#cc9900"]; // Orange
    Cont [label="Local microVM", color="#86b300", fontcolor="#86b300"]; // Purple
    VM   [label="Cloud options",        color="#008080", fontcolor="#008080"]; // Red
    
    // Bottom spacers for outer columns (to balance Convenience and Security)
    node [shape=point, width=0, height=0, style=invis];
    b_Conv; b_Sec;

    // --- Layout Grid Constraints ---

    // Build the 5 Vertical Columns (Forces perfect center alignments)
    // Col 1 (Far left): Convenience directly above the left arrow tip
    { rank=same; Conv -> p_Start -> b_Conv [style=invis]; }
    
    // Col 2, 3, 4 (Middle): Technologies tucked inside the arrow's length
    { rank=same; t_OS -> p_OS -> OS [style=invis]; }
    { rank=same; t_Cont -> p_Cont -> Cont [style=invis]; }
    { rank=same; t_VM -> p_VM -> VM [style=invis]; }
    
    // Col 5 (Far right): Security directly above the right arrow tip
    { rank=same; Sec -> p_End -> b_Sec [style=invis]; }

    // Build the 3 Horizontal Rows
    Conv -> t_OS -> t_Cont -> t_VM -> Sec [style=invis];
    p_Start -> p_OS -> p_Cont -> p_VM -> p_End [style=invis];
    b_Conv -> OS -> Cont -> VM -> b_Sec [style=invis];

    // --- Draw the Visible Arrow ---
    // Connects the far-left point to the far-right point.
    p_Start -> p_End [dir=both, penwidth=1.5, color="gray35", constraint=false];
}
```

## What about containers? {.center}

Containers were not designed with the goal of sandboxing

Many containers require root privilege rendering them inadequate

Apptainer (rootless, with transient sandbox directories and immutable image format) is better but the kernel is shared with the host

## VMs {.center}

## Built-in tools {.center}

TLDR: VERY WEAK

YOLO ("You Only Live Once") mode removes all guardrails

### Sandbox in the harness

codex on by default (macOS: Uses the built-in Seatbelt framework.
Windows (PowerShell): Uses the native Windows sandbox.
Linux / WSL2: Uses Landlock/seccomp or bubblewrap (bwrap).)
claude code can be turned on

### Command hooks

Can be bypassed by alternative tools

- OS-level sandboxes

[seccomp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seccomp) (Linux)
Landlock (Linux)
bubblewrap (Linux)
Seatbelt (macOS)
